- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model tends to overshoot and then gradually correct — but often lags the true peak by 1–3 days.
- Model shows diminishing mean reversion after the 15–20 day mark, failing to adjust downward when true prices stabilize or decline.
- Forecast tends to be overly smooth — underestimates volatility and sudden reversals, especially near the end of the 30-day window.
- When true prices dip below 70 after a spike, model often fails to recognize the correction and continues upward.
- Model exhibits “late correction” bias — true price corrections occur earlier than model’s downward shift, suggesting model is too slow to react to new information.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to “overfitting” recent trends — model follows recent highs too closely, ignoring longer-term mean or seasonal patterns.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or market events that cause sudden price drops — e.g., when true price drops below 70 after a spike, model often doesn’t adjust downward quickly enough.
